dispositions.reason: Step 4 must look the invoice up with principal.orgId only; an organization read from the request body lets any admin reach another organization's invoices, which AC-4 forbids.
Remove the parent/child delegation from step 4: the SPEC states no organization hierarchy and none exists in the plan's own scope, so it is unrequested scope. Same edit as G1-1.

Step 7 must say how refundKeys is read so header text such as constructor or __proto__ cannot match inherited members: an own-property check (Object.hasOwn) or a null-prototype map, and the migration/test must match.

Step 2 must say the existing version-1 migration test's expected schemaVersion is updated to 3 (and declare that edit), because the plan's version bump would otherwise break a test the build is told to keep.

The GET /invoices/:id/refunds route and its org scoping have no planned test: add a test to the plan (and its file to Files), or drop the route; the SPEC scope names listing but has no criterion for it.
The Risks section cites a README upgrade line that no step adds: step 11 must add the forward-only upgrade note to the README, or the plan must stop claiming it. A backup step is optional.
The SPEC does not say what a retry with the same key but a different amount should do (return the original, or refuse); the plan cannot choose that behaviour without the SPEC stating it.
Step 8 must type-check reason: a non-string value should give 422 reason_invalid rather than a TypeError that surfaces as 500.

Step 10 must be buildable as written: pass headers from the handler context rather than req.headers, and state how the route reads replayed to choose 200 or 201 and whether it is in the response body.

Minor tidy-up the build does not need: the plan already declares parseMinor-based validation in refunds.js, so one extra small mapping is harmless. Sharing it is optional and invoices.js is in Files if the builder wants it.
